an8.13:1.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing eight factors, a king’s excellent thoroughbred horse is worthy of a king, an accessory of a king, and reckoned as a factor of kingship.
an8.13:1.3: “Here, (1) a king’s excellent thoroughbred horse is well born on both sides,
an8.13:1.5: he is born in whatever area other excellent thoroughbred horses are born.
an8.13:1.6: (2) He respectfully eats whatever food they give him,
an8.13:1.9: (3) He is repelled by sitting down or lying down near feces or urine.
an8.13:1.10: (4) He is mild and pleasant to live with, and he does not agitate other horses.
an8.13:1.11: (5) He reveals his tricks, ploys, gambits, and wiles as they really are to his trainer
an8.13:1.12: so that his trainer can make an effort to stamp them out of him.
an8.13:1.14: ‘Whether or not the other horses carry loads, I myself will carry them.’
an8.13:1.15: (7) When moving, he moves only along a straight path.
an8.13:1.16: (8) He is strong, and he shows his strength right up until the end of his life.
an8.13:1.17: Possessing these eight factors, a king’s excellent thoroughbred horse is worthy of a king, an accessory of a king, and reckoned as a factor of kingship.
an8.13:2.1: “So too, bhikkhus, possessing eight qualities, a bhikkhu is worthy of gifts … an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.
an8.13:2.3: (1) “Here, a bhikkhu is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha, possessed of good conduct and resort, seeing danger in minute faults. Having undertaken the training rules, he trains in them.
an8.13:2.4: (2) He respectfully eats whatever food they give him,
an8.13:2.7: (3) He is repelled by bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct;
an8.13:2.8: he is repelled by the acquisition of the numerous kinds of bad unwholesome qualities.
an8.13:2.9: (4) He is mild and pleasant to live with, and he does not agitate other bhikkhus.
an8.13:2.10: (5) He reveals his tricks, ploys, gambits, and wiles as they really are to the Teacher or to his wise fellow monks
an8.13:2.11: so that they can make an effort to stamp them out of him.
an8.13:2.12: (6) He is one who takes up the training, determined:
an8.13:2.13: ‘Whether or not other bhikkhus train, I will train.’
an8.13:2.14: (7) When moving, he moves only along a straight path.
an8.13:2.15: In this connection, this is the straight path:
an8.13:2.18: ‘Willingly, let only my skin, sinews, and bones remain, and let the flesh and blood dry up in my body, but I will not relax my energy so long as I have not attained what can be attained by manly strength, energy, and exertion.’
an8.13:2.19: Possessing these eight qualities, a bhikkhu is worthy of gifts … an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.”
